pancake.prep: Lightly grease the pan with a little butter or oil and wipe off any excess.
pancake.cook: Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, leaving space between them. Cook over medium heat for about {time} in total: until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip once.
pancake.check: Both sides should be golden and the center should feel springy, not wet.
notes: Keep the heat at medium - too hot burns the outside before the center cooks.
The first pancake is a test: adjust the heat after it.
Keep finished pancakes warm on a rack in a 95°C / 200°F oven.

recipes.name: Classic Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy diner-style pancakes with golden edges.

less.note: Pancakes use only a little sugar for flavor and browning, so you can halve it with very little effect on the batter. The toppings usually supply the sweetness.
expectedChanges: Barely noticeable difference in the batter

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the egg, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Rest the Batter
steps.text: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while you get the pan ready. This gives fluffier pancakes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with your favorite toppings.

tips: Do not overmix - lumpy batter makes tender pancakes.
Flip when the surface is covered in bubbles and the edges look dry.
Wipe the pan between batches if it starts to smoke.

recipes.name: Banana Pancakes
recipes.description: Soft pancakes with mashed banana mixed right into the batter.

less.note: Ripe banana already sweetens the batter, so the added sugar can be cut by half.
expectedChanges: Barely noticeable difference thanks to the banana

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, mash the banana well, then whisk in the egg, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Rest the Batter
steps.text: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while you get the pan ready. This gives fluffier pancakes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with your favorite toppings.

tips: Use very ripe bananas - they mash easily and taste sweeter.
Banana batter browns faster, so keep the heat at medium-low if needed.
These pancakes are tender; flip them gently.

recipes.name: Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Fluffy pancakes dotted with juicy blueberries.

less.note: Blueberries bring their own sweetness and the toppings add more, so the batter sugar can be halved.
expectedChanges: Barely noticeable difference in the batter

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the egg, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Rest the Batter
steps.text: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while you get the pan ready. This gives fluffier pancakes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with your favorite toppings.

tips: Sprinkle the berries onto the pancakes right after pouring the batter so they do not burst in the bowl.
Frozen blueberries work well - use them straight from the freezer.
Lower the heat slightly if the berries start to burn.

recipes.name: Chocolate Pancakes
recipes.description: Cocoa-rich pancakes that taste like breakfast dessert.

less.note: Cocoa is bitter, so these keep more sugar than other pancakes - about 25% less is the safe reduction.
expectedChanges: Pancakes may look a little paler

steps.title: Mix Dry Ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cocoa powder, sugar, baking powder and salt.

steps.title: Mix Wet Ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the egg, milk, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.

steps.title: Rest the Batter
steps.text: Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while you get the pan ready. This gives fluffier pancakes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm with your favorite toppings.

tips: Chocolate pancakes are hard to judge by color - check that the edges are set and bubbles have popped.
Use medium-low heat; cocoa batter scorches easily.
Sift the cocoa to avoid dry lumps.
